skill.name: commit
skill.description: Helps write conventional commit messages, create atomic commits, and follow git best practices. Use when the agent needs to help with git commits, commit message writing, or git workflow guidance.
skill.summary: Helps create clear conventional commits and guides safe git workflows.

content.value_statement: Developers often lose time turning staged changes into clear commit history. This skill guides Conventional Commits, atomic changes, and safe git review steps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews git status and staged diff output before drafting a message.
Applies Conventional Commits type, scope, subject, body, and footer guidance.
Encourages one logical change per commit.
Uses the included commit template for consistent structure.
Identifies safe git commands and avoids interactive commit workflows.
Requires confirmation before final commit or push.
limitations: Does not replace human review of staged changes.
Does not automate interactive git operations.
Does not allow force pushes or amend operations without explicit user guidance.
Depends on accurate git status and staged diff output.

use_cases.title: Prepare feature commits
use_cases.description: Turn staged feature changes into a clear Conventional Commits message with subject, optional body, and footer guidance.

use_cases.title: Keep team history consistent
use_cases.description: Apply shared commit types and atomic commit rules across routine repository work.

use_cases.title: Document non-code updates
use_cases.description: Create concise commit messages for documentation, configuration, and maintenance changes.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a commit message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest one Conventional Commits message. Keep the subject under 50 characters.

prompt_templates.title: Check commit scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Use git status and git diff --staged to identify the best type and optional scope. Explain the choice before suggesting the message.

prompt_templates.title: Plan atomic commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the staged and unstaged changes. Recommend separate atomic commits with file groups and proposed messages before any commit is created.

prompt_templates.title: Validate release commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the final message for Conventional Commits format, breaking-change footer quality, body clarity, and safe git workflow before commit creation.

output_examples.input: Staged files update login validation and add tests.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: fix(auth): reject invalid login payloads. Body notes validation behavior and added tests.
Suggested message: docs(readme): clarify setup steps. The output keeps the subject concise and omits an unnecessary body.

output_examples.input: A public API option was renamed and migration notes were added.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(api): rename config option. Footer explains the breaking change and migration path.

best_practices: Review staged diff output before writing the final message.
Keep each commit focused on one logical change.
Ask for confirmation before creating or pushing commits.
anti_patterns: Committing changes that were not reviewed.
Using vague subjects such as update files or misc changes.
Force pushing, amending, or rebasing without explicit approval.

faq.question: Which commit format does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Conventional Commits with type, optional scope, subject, body, and footer guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It guides commit creation, but it requires confirmation before final commit or push.

faq.question: Can it help split large changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It encourages atomic commits and can recommend separate logical commits before creation.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it inspect unstaged changes?
faq.answer: It can review git status and staged diff guidance, but the final message should match staged changes.

faq.question: Can it handle breaking changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes BREAKING CHANGE footer guidance and migration context when needed.
